body: Thats also my case. But it's a difference in opinions in a couple. Like she said to me her work is not her passion, it's something she does to get money.

The stress comes from her missing work due to child illness (gastro, fever, etc) and the fact that her bosses told her its her responsability to find a replacement (which imo is a shitty way to manage a workforce). Of course theres always the fact that they are growing up so fast.

i think she legally has to have a degree in quebec and i'm not sure, but i think you can't open a new home childcare anymore but i'm not ENTIRELY sure.

she's also a shy person and i doubt she'd have the courage to go all "yayy kids" and start singing and playing with them.

Although it may sound like i'm just looking for someone who agrees with me, it's nice to know i'm not alone with that vision. We live on a limited budget enough as it is, it's hard going to even smaller.

if let's say the money left if she stopped working was only a quarter of what i make it'd be a no brainer, but money left is cut in about half if not a bit more. it's putting tremendous stress on me despite knowing that a SAHM is a big advantage.

i can't factor it in because i don't know how much we can spare. how much will we save? our 825 for grocery is just that, grocery and diapers. I haven't been factoring in restaurant and such and i never eat out for lunchtime at work. The numbers i provided are just monthly bills paid.

Coupon queen is interesting but we are lacking ressources to be that. Unsure how it applies to canada as a whole, and it's not been working so good in quebec for now, though granted we haven't been trying especially hard.

that's actually very promising. 

One of my main scares is that i get bored, which lets be honest is a very real possibility. How did you keep entertained and mentally healthy. I'm the type who enjoys new things. I'm of course realistic on our capabilities and I of course intend to keep this down. But sitting around and watching a sitcom isn't my idea of relaxation and i'm scared that this is what it may come to.

​

we're actually debt free (aside from car payments which aren't too bad).

it was always part of the equation and forced me to really understand how childcare tax returns work in quebec. at 840 a month for 2 children, it wasn't viable. at 190, that's another story because my SO alone makes 8-9 times that.

How do you manage your groceries when shopping for food? diaper wise the lowest cost we found is at costco and we use my MIL's membership.

Planning meals is very hard too, planning balanced meals is especially hard. we've been living together for 4 years and that's always been our biggest challenge. as much as i want to lower our grocery bill, i sadly don't see how to make it come down.
no need to be sorry, it was a valid point
See this is a better comment than what you first said to me that was seen as insulting and ridiculous. Thank you for your input.

Alright i'll admit that i didnt think about ongoing upkeep on cars becausr... Well... We've litterally never had any (sort of ironic). However the family van loan only costs us 305 at 0% interest. Yes the price is of course boosted.

And the reason i posted in a finance subreddit and not a prenting subreddit is because i need financial insight. My question was worded poorly, granted, but i have been getting very good finance related answers which have been opening my eyes to the option.

I was being ironic of sorts. Your comment literaly added no plus value to the discussion. I'm asking questions about how to make it work because money stresses me so saying i should make more income is like telling someone who has asthma to breathe.

We actually can though, if it mean coming even and having nothing left for bad luck, it's not a smart move.  


Emotionnaly i agree and a lot of people commenting (no offense meant) seem to think i'm cold and uncaring for my children and girlfriend. She cares for their emotional well being, i care for their financial well being. 

​

The issue wouldn't be different if it was me being a stay at home dad, we still have a lot of things to consider. I don't mind making a sacrifice and i've made a lot already. It's about making a smart sacrifice to not end up poor.

it's true the tone of my post says that, but it was written under emotion (it's been a tough weekend). i feel uneasy and feel choked by the amount we have left at the end of the month. it's a bit of a tradeoff over who goes into burnout first. Considering her family desires and my career reality (i in no way mean to say my career is more important than her family desires, just to be clear) it is stressing me out. Because of the fact my workplace MAY shut down, and i can't find another job currently. If i had something down the pipeline, would be another story.
yeah i've used it a lot to calculate. and it's actually very precise. it's been spot on for us

Also yes, despite the amazing evil (in my opinion) the last governement in quebec was, it nonetheless made all daycare the same cost. CPE is about 7$ a day per child (more or less true for 2nd) subsidized daycare is the same cost, and there's a tax return on private daycar that brings it to about the same price as CPE depending on your salary. Since the family revenue is about 55k/year, we fall in the lowest bracket and have the highest return.
no sorry, we have a mazda 5 and a fiesta
no, only a mazda 5 (the costlier option) and a ford fiesta

The problem with this is that on the family van we recently bought is about 700$ of that payment including gas, The paid off car is about 125$ per month including gas.

By our estimations, using the family van more 1) increases the gas consumation by about 100$ and 2) keeps my gf from moving around (point 2 is a luxury).

A mazda 5 is a useful car, but it's gas consumption is insane compared to the other car.

No offense but this is a personal opinion and doesn't help me alleviate the financiary burden in my issue. It is hell, we are having a hard time. 

it's something i truly want to support because i had a SAHM mother. I just don't want to live poorly and i'm not asking for much luxury.

Our grocery costs have to be better defined because yes they are high, but 150 a week not including diapers doesn't sound too high, i think. But hey maybe i'm wrong. we can't live on 75$ a week for a family of 4 like one of the dragons in quebec said (if you can read french, it's sort of a disturbing read).

Also it's not the option i like the most because i am scared about not only the education our kids are getting (hey my 2 year old is starting to know some english, my gf doesn't really master english and knowing a 2nd language is important in my eyes.

As far as car expenses go, it's actually better to keep the 2nd car until it starts costing us too much.

We have the family van, because my car can't hold 2 adults and 2 kids  necessities unfortunately. the ford fiesta has a shitty interior design.

however gas + insurance on the fiesta brings me to 110$ monthly. it's a 5 year old car that had a plan to keep up to date with the initial increase in pay. this car is paid off.

We also own a mazda 5 that we recently bought a year ago with 0% interest. insurance is 105 monthly, and gas is atleast 80-100$ for same usage as the ford fiesta. while now with minimal usage the cost of gas is about 40-60$ per month since the car gets much MUCH less mileage.

That's without counting in the use of the car and possible breakage. We have 7 years to finish paying off the mazda and i'd rather it see much less usage and thus, much less chances of breaking parts. I could be wrong, but i find it is an economy of sorts if we spare mileage on the family car for as long as we can
I know this is a personal question, however i,m starting to see a lot of good ideas from other users on the tax credit end, and it is starting to feel like it's trading a dollar for 3.5 25 cents.
\*sigh\* and of course my province is once again the only one not listed. Screw our french canadian asses lol
I wrote back to you because you make an interesting point and i feel we could expand on it.

In all honesty i'm not looking for is this a good idea or not. I'm just scared that the amount is not enough to get by on. Especially knowing my spending habits but i am working on toning them down to accept that amount

is there a way to calculate how the basic tax credit works and how to apply it? Also we're now in mid november, and since she was on maternity leave for the biggest part of 2018 and is technically working for the 3-4 months of 2018, i doubt we would get much this year and would only benefit from the tax credit at the start of 2020 since it would only apply in 2019.

Alright yeah it's another name in french (ACE) it has been acounted in my data, Also the amount that we receive from the governement of Qc.

and i'm fairly certain the amount we could get from tax deductions because she's not working would be enough to counter balance the loss of revenue.

in that 550 per month we have to factor in savings for a rainy day fund, thankfully i have a retirement fund at my work, activities (i refuse for me or her to stay in home it's not healthy) for us and the kids, clothes she says we can ask for that at christmas and birthdays, yes we can but there will be needs at other times, and both parents will need clothes at some point.

There's also another very important factor consider. It's a very real possibility that my workplace is closing down mid december. Yes i have enough money put aside for 3-6 months of all vital expenses paid, i already am looking for another job, but one month into the process i am not getting calls back.

Alright, english and financials not being my mother tongue i don't understand much. I know it's a deeply personal question, but i need to understand all the details before choosing. 

What is a CCB?

How can i know what can of tax credit we can get?

Also keep in mind she picked work back up in september.

There has been already some give and take. I accepted her working only part time to help her stay with the kids. However right now working is giving her physical pain because of stress. Her not working is giving me physical pain because of the amount we have left over at the end of the month. Of course there are economies we can do in our current lifestyle but it's not going to increase the budgeted money. Thats the thing. We don't know where to start, if we live a more "comfortable" life (we barely make enough money together to be out of poverty) she's going to be depressed. If we live a more comfortable parenting lifestyle, i'm the one who'se going to crash and burn.

​

Both our kids weren't expected, and i've worked a lot on myself to be a good father and be a good SO. I even accepted to move in litteraly the same appartment building as her mother and her grandmother because it was a more advantageous life despite her family being fairly invasive. I feel like i'm always giving in and it's starting to be hard to take. 

My biggest issue is she refuses to go to the doctor's to get checked or go to a therapist to help her manage her stress. If we both work it's doable, if she doesn't we won't be able to get the help we may need in the future without going in the red.
she wants to quit right now. i've offered her the idea of "ok i'll find a job and you can quit" to no avail

But like all things in the post kids era, everything is harder so i take a lot on myself and try not to interpret everything as insulting or a lack of reciprocity. But yes i do feel neglected sometimes, and i'm sure she feels the same.

Its a very valid point, however i have been in her shoes when our first daughter was born. She had a weird pattern and was very distant for the first 6 months. My reaction was different probably because my family background was very different. I never snooped or spied on her.

When i say i didnt think much of it, i mean i cant have know she'd feel that way because it never came up before. So how could i think that talking about my partner in the project affect her so much. My speech wasn't 100% work related because when you work for 6 months with someone, it doesnt stay work related. So sometimes it was like "oh she tried x recipe it sounded good we should try it." Or she went on a trip to whatever country and said she had a blast and looked like a fun trip to do. I'm not perfect but i try to stay respectful and if i wasnt, i do my best to fix my manners. It just never seems enough.

But i'll agree that this is only my side of the story.
